A0261.title: Synthetic Market Signal Detection
A0261.definition: Detect non-organic market signals generated by AI, coordinated accounts, false data sources, or model poisoning before they enter research and trading decision chains.
A0261.description:
Synthetic market signal detection collects synchronization among news, research reports, social media, order books, trades, on-chain data, sentiment indicators, and model outputs to identify abnormal signals generated by AI, amplified by coordinated accounts, injected by false data sources, or caused by retrieval-data pollution. Cross-source consistency, text similarity, account graphs, time-series bursts, and model-explanation drift help judge whether a signal formed organically.

This control applies to AI investment agent manipulation, market information manipulation, and investor cognition manipulation. It should gate research summaries, automated strategy signals, and trading-agent inputs, then down-rank, isolate, or escalate suspicious signals for human review.
A0261.limitation: Real breaking events can also burst across sources, causing false positives. Attackers can mix real news, small real trades, or real account reposts to increase credibility. Authoritative disclosure, trading behavior, and post-event review are needed.
